doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Metronome All-Stars 1949-50, Stan Getz, and the Miles Davis bootleg
summary: He recalls the 1950 All-Stars with Getz, and a Royal Roost broadcast billing him with Miles.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: So in ’49 and ’50 you had your fourth Metronome All-Stars with Lennie Tristano, Lee Konitz, Dizzy, Max Roach…
Oh, that’s right, Stan was on that one, yeah, great player, too.
Yep, I can remember that. You know, not exactly, but pretty much.
Had you ever worked with him before, played with him before?

You had. DeFranco:…yeah, we played some sessions together. And I believe we were on, there was one recording done, from a broadcast—a bootleg—with Stan and I. And also with Miles Davis and I and I used to tell people for years that I never played with Miles Davis.
But at the Royal Roost the announcer Symphony Sid said, “Here is Buddy DeFranco and Miles Davis.” And it became a bootleg record.
